title: LiteLLM Helm Chart Values
description: Configuration values for the LiteLLM proxy Helm chart

image.description: LiteLLM proxy container image (must be the -database variant for in-boot migrations)

repository.description: Image repository. Must stay a litellm *-database image: the plain litellm image has no Prisma and cannot run the DB migrations this chart relies on

tag.description: Image tag; falls back to .Chart.AppVersion when empty

pullPolicy.description: Image pull policy (IfNotPresent, Always or Never)

type.description: Service type. ClusterIP keeps the proxy internal; LoadBalancer or NodePort exposes the admin UI and key-management API, so front it with auth first

port.description: Port the proxy listens on and the Service publishes; also serves /metrics

storeModelInDB.description: Persist models added through the admin UI / API into Postgres so they survive restarts

logLevel.description: LITELLM_LOG level, e.g. DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR

metrics.description: Prometheus ServiceMonitor scraping LiteLLM's /metrics on the proxy port

enabled.description: Render the ServiceMonitor that scrapes LiteLLM's /metrics

proxy_config.description: Rendered verbatim to /etc/litellm/config.yaml; at least one model is required to boot

model_list.description: Models the proxy exposes. Each entry needs model_name plus litellm_params (model, api_key). Reference credentials as api_key: os.environ/<VAR> and supply <VAR> via apiKeys or extraEnvFrom. At least one model is required to boot

general_settings.description: LiteLLM general_settings block. Keep master_key: os.environ/PROXY_MASTER_KEY - dropping it leaves the admin UI and key-management API unauthenticated

masterkey.description: Proxy master key (PROXY_MASTER_KEY) used to authenticate admin UI and key-management calls

value.description: Set the master key explicitly instead of letting the chart generate one, so it is reproducible and can be handed to callers up front. Ignored when existingSecret is set

existingSecret.description: Use a pre-created master-key secret instead of a chart-managed one. Required for GitOps, where the lookup that preserves a generated key may not run

secretKey.description: Key within the master-key secret to read. Must match the key name inside existingSecret when you bring your own

apiKeys.description: Provider API keys managed by this chart, as VAR: value (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY: sk-...). Each becomes a key in a chart-owned secret mounted via envFrom, so api_key: os.environ/<VAR> resolves without creating a secret by hand

extraEnvFrom.description: Existing secrets (by secretName) mounted via envFrom, e.g. holding provider API keys or a DATABASE_URL when postgres.enabled is false

extraEnv.description: Extra plain environment variables as VAR: value. These land unencrypted in the Deployment, so put credentials in apiKeys or extraEnvFrom instead

resources.description: CPU/memory requests and limits for the proxy container

requests.description: Guaranteed CPU/memory reserved for the proxy container

cpu.description: CPU request, e.g. 500m. Boot runs Prisma migrations alongside the Python proxy, so too small a request makes startup slow enough to trip the startup probe

memory.description: Memory request, e.g. 1Gi. LiteLLM's own guidance is a 1Gi floor

limits.description: Hard CPU/memory ceiling for the proxy container

cpu.description: CPU limit in millicores, e.g. 2000m. Headroom above the request lets the Prisma migration burst on boot

memory.description: Memory limit, e.g. 2Gi. Below ~1.5Gi the container is OOM-killed during the Prisma-plus-proxy boot spike

replicaCount.description: Number of proxy pods to run. LiteLLM keeps no local state, so this is safe to raise. Ignored when autoscaling.enabled is true, because the HorizontalPodAutoscaler then owns the replica count

enabled.description: Enable the HorizontalPodAutoscaler. Multiple replicas need Redis to share rate-limit and spend state

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description: Average CPU utilization percentage the autoscaler targets

postgres.description: zopdev/postgres subchart providing the backing database

enabled.description: Deploy the bundled postgres subchart. Turn off to bring your own database, then supply a Prisma-compatible DATABASE_URL through a secret listed in extraEnvFrom

services.description: Databases the postgres subchart creates (name/database). Internal wiring: the proxy's DATABASE_URL secret name is derived from the first entry
